# Skills reference

Generated from `skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter. Each skill works on its own (`npx skills add furkansarikaya/proofline --skill <name>`).

| Skill | Description | Version |
|---|---|---|
| `api-design` | Designs or changes API contracts. Uses the project's existing contract format when one exists (OpenAPI/Swagger, GraphQL SDL, protobuf, JSON Schema) and edits that; writes docs/design/API.md only when no contract exists. Covers endpoints (METHOD /path), request/response shapes, errors, auth, idempotency, pagination and versioning, and flags every breaking and every versioned-contract change so the lead can name it in PLAN "## Contracts". Also reverse-engineers the contract documentation from existing code on "/proofline design api". Use when a task adds or changes an API surface. | 0.0.41 |
| `concurrency-proof` | Concurrency review of a change (working tree, branch, pull request or proofline run) that reports only proven problems. Finds the shared state and critical sections the diff touches (races, deadlock, lost update, double processing, idempotency, retry side effects, message ordering and redelivery, timeouts, transaction boundaries, lock lifecycle), proves each risk with a concrete interleaving traced step by step across at least two actors with file:line per step, and reproduces it with concurrent or repeated runs in the project's own test runner when the project allows (else reproduction is stated UNSUPPORTED). PASS means no proven problem, never that the code is free of concurrency defects; examined but unproven risks are listed separately. Used by the Reviewer for the REVIEW `concurrency` focus, or standalone on request. | 0.0.41 |
| `contract-proof` | Proves backward and forward compatibility of changed API, event and data contracts (OpenAPI/Swagger, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, GraphQL SDL, protobuf, whichever the repository has). Uses a compatibility tool the project or machine already has; otherwise a dependency-free built-in structural diff (JSON and a safe YAML subset with $ref resolution; a conservative line-level diff for GraphQL SDL and protobuf); a format it cannot parse is UNSUPPORTED, never a pass. Classifies every change breaking, non-breaking or needs-review by a rule id with the request/response direction, lists the in-repo consumers from the evidence-map impact report (consumers outside the repository are unknown), and fails a breaking change that PLAN.md `## Contracts` does not cover with versioning, migration or deprecation. Run by the Reviewer for the REVIEW `contract` focus (REVIEW_RULES, REVIEW_SMALL on tier small) or standalone on request. | 0.0.41 |
| `data-design` | Designs the data side of a change for the project's actual database - data model, Mermaid ERD, invariants, and a migration plan with expand/contract steps, batched idempotent resumable backfill, reversibility and rollback per step, lock risk per statement, and a data-loss assessment. Classifies every planned or implemented statement mechanically (scripts/classify-migration.mjs); a destructive migration makes the task CRITICAL and stops for user approval. Also reverse-engineers docs/design/DATA_MODEL.md from an existing schema, and, as the REVIEW_DATA focus, checks implemented migrations against the frozen PLAN "## Data" and validates them on the test suite's own throwaway database (UNSUPPORTED without one). Use when persistence or schema changes, on "/proofline design data", or for a data review gate. | 0.0.41 |
| `debug-proof` | Debugs a failure with proof instead of guesses. Reproduces the bug with a failing command or test, lists ranked falsifiable hypotheses, narrows with logging, input bisection and `git bisect run` (in a worktree) when a known-good commit exists, proves the root cause with an experiment that flips the failure by changing only the cause, applies the minimal fix, and adds a regression test that fails before and passes after. Keeps a ledger of every experiment and outcome. Covers build-error resolution. Never reports "fixed" without the regression test. Use for bugs, failing tests, crashes and build or compile errors, or on "/proofline debug". | 0.0.41 |
| `design-sync` | Checks durable design documents against the code and reports drift as `doc:line -> missing code fact` - every table in DATA_MODEL.md exists in the schema or migrations, every path in ARCHITECTURE.md exists, every endpoint in API.md (or an OpenAPI file) exists in the routes, every token and component named in DESIGN.md exists where the doc says. Also reverse-engineers those documents from existing code (system, data, api, ui). Use in the verify gate, standalone with --check, or as a first step in a project that has code but no design docs. Heuristic misses are reported as unverifiable, never as drift. | 0.0.41 |
| `docs-writer` | Writes and maintains project documentation that matches the code and follows a writing profile. Mode create writes a document from scratch, mode update takes a diff or commit range and updates every document it makes stale, mode audit checks all documents and fixes them. An evidence script proves that the commands, file paths, flags, config keys and repo-internal links a document quotes exist in the project, and a length script measures sentence and paragraph length under the config block writing. Use when a task changes user-visible behaviour, or on /proofline docs create, update or audit. | 0.0.41 |
| `evidence-map` | Bounded codebase investigation that returns compact, verified evidence. Takes one assignment (objective, allowed scope, expected output, stop condition) and maps the live implementation, its callers, tests, patterns to follow, dependencies, constraints, affected files, regression risk and conflicting or dead duplicate implementations. Every claim is a `path:symbol` or `path:line` checked by reading or grepping; unverifiable statements are dropped or listed as open questions. A bundled script mechanically re-verifies every claim before the result is returned. Also defines how the lead consolidates several Explorer results into EVIDENCE.md. `impact` mode: a JSON report of what changed symbols reach (references, modules, contracts, tests) with stated limits. Use before planning a change in unfamiliar code, or when the proofline lead dispatches an Explorer. | 0.0.41 |
| `explain-html` | Explains a topic, a task, a review or a completion report as one self-contained HTML page with inline SVG diagrams, inline CSS and JS, a light and a dark theme, and no network request. A small validator rejects any external reference, a missing title and a page over the size limit. Use on /proofline explain <topic\|TASK-ID>, or when the user wants a page they can open in a browser to understand something. | 0.0.41 |
| `exploit-proof` | Defensive security review of a change in the user's own repository (working tree, branch or pull request) before merge. Enumerates the entry points the diff touches, follows untrusted data to sensitive sinks (SQL and query builders, shell, filesystem paths, HTML output, outbound URL fetches, deserializers, authorization decisions, secrets and crypto), tries to refute every candidate, and reports only confirmed vulnerabilities - traced (concrete input, file:line per hop, why each guard fails) or reproduced (a regression test in the project's own test framework, run in a throwaway git worktree). Everything else is a suspicion. Its `dependencies` focus audits new or changed dependencies: a manifest diff against the plan's `## Dependencies`, the license policy from config, and known vulnerabilities only from the project's own audit tool output (nothing installed, no model-memory CVE lookup). Used by the Security Reviewer for the SECURITY gate (any finding -> FAIL, never waivable) or standalone on request. | 0.0.41 |
| `intent-grill` | Interviews the user about a vague or high-stakes request before a task is written. Builds a tree of the open decisions (scope, behavior, data, UI, failure modes, non-goals), asks one question at a time in dependency order with options, a recommended answer and why, never answers on the user's behalf, and stops when every branch is resolved or explicitly deferred by the user. Writes INTENT.md (decisions with who decided each, deferred items, acceptance-criteria and out-of-scope candidates) that feeds task-author and plan-contract. Use for COMPLEX or CRITICAL requests, when a request leaves behavior open, or when the user asks to be grilled ("/proofline task --grill"). | 0.0.41 |
| `llm-wiki` | Keeps a persistent, Git-backed Markdown wiki under docs/wiki that grows with the project instead of rediscovering facts on every question. Ingests sourced knowledge (a session summary under raw/sessions, a canonical document) into source, entity, concept, decision and lesson pages joined by [[wikilinks]], answers questions from the wiki, and lints it (missing or dangling source, invalid status, contradicted page without contradicts, duplicate title, broken wikilink, orphan) into lint-report.md without fixing anything on its own. Never edits raw sources, never deletes a page (outdated pages move to archive/). Serves the Knowledge step of a run (always runs, see KNOWLEDGE.md). Use for a project knowledge base or on "/proofline wiki ingest\|query\|lint". | 0.0.41 |
| `performance-proof` | Proves or refutes a performance regression by measurement, never by reading code. Runs the project's own benchmark command repeatedly in a base worktree and in the change worktree, interleaved, records the environment (OS, CPU count, load, tool versions, command, warmup, runs, timestamps), and lets a bundled dependency-free script compute median, MAD, IQR and a seeded bootstrap interval and decide PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE by a calibrated rule against a threshold (default 10 % on the median; project config, frozen with the plan, and the plan's budget win). Noise is INCONCLUSIVE, never FAIL and never PASS; no benchmark command in the project is UNSUPPORTED, never PASS. Patterns such as N+1 queries that were not measured are reported as judged only. The proofline reviewer runs it for the REVIEW `performance` focus when the plan flags `performance_critical`; also usable on its own. | 0.0.41 |
| `plan-contract` | Writes an executable, scoped PLAN.md for one task and validates it mechanically. YAML `scope:` front matter lists every file the change may touch, each mapped to at least one acceptance criterion; every criterion maps back to a scope path or an explicit test. Adds only the sections the task's class and scope require (Architecture for COMPLEX/CRITICAL, Data with `destructive: yes\|no` when persistence changes, UI when UI changes), plus Behavior, Tests, Verification commands, and explicit Dependencies, Contracts and Assumptions (a risk register; an unverified high-risk entry stops the freeze until the user answers). TDD exemptions need a specific reason. A bundled validator checks mapping both ways, required sections, path existence, globs and duplicates. Use when the proofline lead plans a task before freeze, or standalone to turn a TASK.md into a reviewable plan. | 0.0.41 |
| `product-assess` | Tests the assumptions behind a product plan with the user in the main session - lists the assumptions with risk type, importance and evidence level and marks the riskiest, designs probes whose success and failure thresholds are locked before they run, runs a premortem, has an independent strategy reviewer attack the most-trusted assumptions, records one decision (build, clarify or stop) as a short ADR, and after the build records the outcome against a measured baseline and target. Deterministic scripts check each document, lock probe thresholds with a hash, and re-run the outcome script. Output goes to docs/product/<slug>/. Use when a plan rests on assumptions nobody tested, before a PRD is split into tasks, or after a release to learn from the result (/proofline product assess). | 0.0.41 |
| `product-discovery` | Discovers a product problem with the user in the main session before a PRD exists - frames the problem and its limits, researches the market from a written search plan and sources, runs and synthesises user interviews, profiles competitors beyond a feature table, and lists and ranks opportunities with the evidence behind each - into docs/product/<slug>/ (FRAME, RESEARCH, INTERVIEWS, COMPETITORS, OPPORTUNITIES). Facts are never invented, but the agent proposes assumptions, risks, competitors and questions that the user accepts or rejects; every document ends with insights that name the decision they change. Deterministic scripts reject unsourced numbers, quotes not in the raw interview, stale or unverifiable cells, unanswered search questions, opportunities without evidence and a set without insights. Use when a product idea is still vague or unresearched, or before product-spec, or on request (/proofline product discover). | 0.0.41 |
| `product-spec` | Writes a product requirements document (PRD) with the user in the main session - problem and whose problem it is, goals, non-goals, user stories with acceptance criteria, FR-n and NFR-n requirements, success metrics that say how they are measured, assumptions, a completeness list (error states, permissions, personal data, security, performance, accessibility, languages, analytics, rollout, dependencies), blocking and non-blocking open questions - to docs/product/<slug>/PRD.md. Every claim is marked as a fact with its source, an assumption with its risk type, or a decision with who decided; unknowns never enter the body as fact, and the agent proposes edge cases, assumptions and questions the user did not raise. Deterministic scripts check the PRD, gate its split into tasks, check that tasks cover every requirement, and trace a requirement or task to its tests, run evidence and pull request. Use when a product idea needs a PRD before tasks, or on request (/proofline product, /proofline trace). | 0.0.41 |
| `proof-review` | Reviews a code change (uncommitted work, a branch, or a PR) and reports only what it can prove. Checks that the change does what it says, using claims from the user, the PR description, linked issues and commit messages, never inferred from the code. Checks it against the team's written project rules (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, ADRs), reporting only checkable rules the diff newly breaks. Hunts bugs in the changed code and its direct callers, reporting one only when a temporary test reproduced it in a separate git worktree or a concrete input was traced line by line. No style, naming, suggestions or severity scores. Never fixes code. In a proofline run the intent source is the frozen PLAN.md and a focus parameter (plan, rules, bugs, rules+tests, all, config) selects what is reviewed. Use when the user asks to review a change, PR, branch or uncommitted work with proof, or when the proofline lead dispatches a review focus. | 0.0.41 |
| `proofline-lead` | The proofline lead's lifecycle method for the main session (AGENT_ROLE unset = lead). Takes a request or task through intake, classification, branch and baseline, discovery, design, plan, freeze, one implementer, tiered independent gates, the bounded fix loop, completion report and cleanup, with `agent.sh next` as the single source of the next step. Dispatches each specialist on its configured runtime (Claude Agent tool or dispatch.sh), relays specialist questions verbatim, never writes product code, never records or waives a verdict, and stops for plan approval (supervised), destructive operations, scope changes, commit, push and PR. Consumes only result headers and tables. Serves /proofline, run, resume, queue, task, design, review, audit, debug, deliver and clean. Use as the main session in a project where proofline is installed. | 0.0.41 |
| `proofline` | The user-facing /proofline entry point. `$ARGUMENTS` is the subcommand: init, upgrade, doctor, status (default), queue, clean and version run through the proofline CLI (`bin/proofline`); run, resume, task, design, review, audit, debug, knowledge and deliver hand the session to the proofline-lead skill, which carries each out through `agent.sh` and the specialist roles. Use to install proofline in a project, check that its rules are enforced, or start, resume and deliver a task. | 0.0.41 |
| `qa-plan` | Independent QA in two phases. Before implementation, writes QA_PLAN.md from the task's acceptance criteria - one concrete acceptance scenario per criterion plus adversarial scenarios only for categories that apply, each with how it will be executed. After implementation, executes the frozen plan against the real code and writes QA_REPORT.md with a mechanical PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict; the plan is never weakened after seeing the code. Use for STANDARD and larger tasks, or to QA any change against its stated criteria. | 0.0.41 |
| `system-design` | Designs the smallest valid architecture for a task, or reverse-engineers docs/design/ARCHITECTURE.md from an existing codebase. C4-style levels (context, container, component) only as deep as the change needs, every component mapped to a verified repo path, boundaries, compatibility, migration concerns, trade-offs, and numbered ADRs only for decisions with real alternatives. Writes the PLAN "## Architecture" text and design/ARCHITECTURE.md inside a run. Use for COMPLEX/CRITICAL tasks, when a change crosses component boundaries, or on "/proofline design system". Never designs speculative structure. | 0.0.41 |
| `task-author` | Turns a one-sentence request or an external issue (GitHub, Jira, Linear, markdown) into the canonical TASK.md - goal, context, numbered observable acceptance criteria, explicit out of scope, constraints, risks, suggested class with the indicator that placed it - and renders it into a per-target template (project templates in .agents/templates/tasks/ win over the bundled ones). Use before planning or implementing any non-trivial change, to import a ticket, or to export a task to an issue tracker. Asks the user once when something is ambiguous; never invents requirements. | 0.0.41 |
| `tdd-proof` | Implements a change test-first with recorded proof. For every non-exempt scope path it records RED (the new behaviour's assertion fails, for the right reason), GREEN (the same test passes and nothing else broke) and optional REFACTOR through `agent.sh worker-evidence` in a run, or a local ledger standalone. A compile, type, import, syntax or setup error, a missing file or a runner finding no tests is NOT RED; a minimal stub makes the test compile first. Before GREEN is accepted the production change is reverted or mutated in a separate worktree and the new test must fail again (hollow-test check). Use whenever code is implemented or fixed. | 0.0.41 |
| `test-trust` | Audits how far a test suite can be trusted, using runnable evidence instead of opinion. Finds flaky tests (nondeterministic or order-dependent), hollow tests (stay green when the code they protect is broken, proven by targeted mutation), and slow tests (relative to the scope's own median). Two modes - full audits an explicit scope, diff is the proofline review gate's tests focus (changed tests and tests covering changed units, with a computed PASS or FAIL). Language- and framework-agnostic; discovers how the project runs its tests and proves runner capabilities before relying on them. Reports findings only, never fixes. Use when the user asks "can I trust these tests?", wants a flaky, hollow, or slow test audit of a specific scope, or when the proofline lead dispatches the tests focus of a review. | 0.0.41 |
| `ui-design` | Designs UI work. Reverse-engineers a DESIGN.md design system (tokens, typography, spacing, colour roles, components, accessibility baseline) from the existing UI when it is absent, and writes the per-task UI spec (screens, flows, every state including empty, loading, error, success, partial and permission-denied, copy, keyboard and screen-reader behaviour, responsive rules) that goes into PLAN "## UI" and design/UI.md. Reuses existing tokens and components, verified by path, before inventing new ones. Sets a visitor mode per surface and, for persuade and experience surfaces, an idea, argument, dealt directions, imagery, motion and typography plan; patterns are defaults needing a reason. Adds a grounded creative direction (conform to DESIGN.md; redesign only on the task's request with the user's approval), a UX pattern comparison, a spec self-critique and a per-criterion visual-proof marking; never approves its own design. Use when a task changes UI, or on "/proofline design ui". | 0.0.41 |
| `verify-proof` | Mechanical proof that a frozen plan was implemented - every acceptance criterion has a passing test or, when every mapped PLAN scope path has a tdd_exemption, recorded passing command evidence; changed paths stay inside scope; build, test and lint commands pass. Writes VERIFY.md ending in one Verdict line. | 0.0.41 |
| `visual-proof` | Visual proof of a UI change with the browser tooling the project or machine already has (a project browser-test dependency or an installed headless Chromium-family browser; a runtime browser tool only as an adapter). Measures, per changed screen, state and viewport, overflow, invisible or covered interactive elements, text contrast, touch-target size, focus order and visibility, that every spec state renders, forms, modals, long content, the project's accessibility scanner findings, technical SEO for public pages, plus an optional design group (type scale, empty hero, vacuum, motion, UX rules such as alt text and form labels, image ledger) and a source lint; every measurement carries a selector, value, threshold and a sha256 screenshot. Hierarchy, density, character, a 14-point critique and the judged UX rules never close the gate alone. No tooling means UNSUPPORTED, never PASS. Used by QA or standalone. | 0.0.41 |
